en.name: Molasses
en.summary: An unopened jar of molasses keeps 1–2 years from purchase in the cupboard, and about 6 months once opened. It is thick, dark and very sugary, so it fails by fermenting or growing surface mould rather than by anything dramatic.
en.pantry: Cool, dry and dark, tightly capped: 1–2 years from purchase unopened, and about 6 months after opening. Molasses is concentrated enough to resist most spoilage on its own, but it is not as concentrated as refined syrup — it holds real moisture, and that is enough for yeasts and moulds to work on a diluted surface. The failures are therefore almost always at the neck: a sticky thread of syrup down the outside, a lid that does not seat properly, or a wet spoon dipped straight into the jar. Wipe the rim, cap it hard, and keep it away from the hob, which darkens and stiffens it.
en.fridge: Refrigeration is not required and mostly makes molasses difficult: cold turns it into something you cannot pour and cannot measure, and warming it repeatedly is what encourages crystals and separation. Keep it in the cupboard and work to the opened figure. If your kitchen is very warm and humid and a previous jar fermented on you, then cold will slow that down — stand the jar in hot water for a few minutes before use, and accept that it will always pour slowly.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for molasses, and freezing it is unnecessary. It does not set hard at household freezer temperatures, it simply becomes unworkable, and a capped jar in the cupboard already covers a year or more. If you have bought a catering tin, decant it into small jars and keep those in the cupboard rather than putting the lot in the freezer.
spoilage: Mould at the surface or around the rim and inside the lid.
A fermented, winey or fizzy character, or a lid that is under pressure.
White crystalline grains through the syrup that will not dissolve in warm water.
A sharply sour smell rather than the usual bittersweet, smoky one.
tips: Wipe the rim and thread before capping; that is where a jar goes wrong.
Never dip a used or wet spoon into the jar.
Oil the measuring spoon lightly and the molasses will slide off cleanly.
Buy the size you will actually use within the opened window.

faq.q: How long does molasses keep after opening?
faq.a: About 6 months in a tightly capped jar in a cool dry cupboard. Unopened, 1–2 years from purchase.

faq.q: Does molasses need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No. Cold makes it almost impossible to pour. Keep it capped in a cupboard unless your kitchen is very warm and humid.

faq.q: How can you tell if molasses has gone bad?
faq.a: Mould at the rim or surface, a fermented or fizzy smell, or a pressurised lid. Thickening and darkening alone are normal.

zh.name: 糖蜜
zh.summary: 未開封的糖蜜從購買日起算放櫥櫃可放 1～2 年，開封後約 6 個月。它濃稠、深色、糖度很高，所以壞掉的方式是發酵或表面長霉，不會有什麼戲劇性的變化。
zh.pantry: 陰涼、乾燥、避光，蓋子旋緊：未開封自購買日起 1～2 年，開封後約 6 個月。糖蜜的濃度足以自己擋掉大部分的腐敗，但它畢竟不像精製糖漿那麼濃——它保有真正的水分，而那點水分就夠讓酵母和霉菌在被稀釋的表面上工作。所以失敗幾乎都發生在瓶口：外側掛著一條黏糖漿、蓋子沒有旋正，或者把沾濕的湯匙直接伸進去。請擦乾淨瓶口、蓋緊，並遠離爐台，高溫會讓它變深、變硬。
zh.fridge: 糖蜜不需要冷藏，而且冷藏多半只會帶來麻煩：低溫會讓它變成倒不出來、量不準的東西，而反覆回溫又正好是造成結晶和分離的原因。請放櫥櫃，並以開封後的期限為準。如果你的廚房又熱又濕、上一罐真的發酵過，那低溫確實能拖慢它——用之前先把罐子泡熱水幾分鐘，並接受它永遠倒得很慢這件事。
zh.freezer: 糖蜜沒有公布的冷凍期限，也沒有冷凍的必要。家用冷凍庫的溫度不會讓它結成硬塊，只會讓它變得完全不能用；而蓋好的罐子放櫥櫃本來就能撐一年以上。如果買的是營業用大桶，請分裝成小罐放櫥櫃，而不是整桶塞冷凍。
spoilage: 表面、瓶口或蓋子內側長霉。
有發酵味、酒味或氣泡感，或蓋子明顯有壓力。
糖漿中出現泡熱水也化不開的白色結晶顆粒。
聞起來是尖銳的酸味，而不是原本苦甜帶煙燻的味道。
tips: 蓋回去之前先擦乾淨瓶口與螺紋，罐子都是從那裡壞掉的。
不要把用過或沾濕的湯匙伸進罐子。
量匙先抹一層薄油，糖蜜就會乾淨地滑下來。
買你在開封期限內用得完的容量。

faq.q: 糖蜜開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 蓋緊放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃約 6 個月。未開封則是自購買日起 1～2 年。
不用。低溫會讓它幾乎倒不出來。除非廚房又熱又濕，否則蓋好放櫥櫃就好。
瓶口或表面長霉、有發酵或氣泡感、蓋子脹氣。單純變稠變深是正常的。
